details: This package is a republished WhatsApp automation library shipped under an unofficial scope while presenting itself as a fork of the canonical @whiskeysockets/baileys library. Injected into lib/Socket/newsletter.js is a connection.update listener that, every time a client session reaches connection === 'open', silently issues a FOLLOW request (xwa2_newsletter_join_v2) for the hardcoded channel 120363417337256584@newsletter. The library's own API requires the caller to name a channel for any follow action, so this enrolment is not user-initiated: any application built on the package subscribes its WhatsApp account to that channel on login without prompting. The success handler then logs a different channel identifier, 120363203083379699@newsletter, so that anyone auditing logs is told a channel other than the one actually joined. No external command-and-control host is present: all traffic goes to WhatsApp's own service (whatsapp[.]net / s[.]whatsapp[.]net), and no credentials, tokens, environment variables or.npmrc contents are read or transmitted by the package. The only anomalous network behaviour is the unauthorized channel enrolment itself.
